nodes.text: Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence. Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence with $n_{k+1}/n_k \geq c>1$. Must\[\sum_k\frac{1}{F_{n_k}}\]be irrational?

#267 : [ErGr80,p.65] irrationality It may be sufficient to have $n_k/k\to \infty$. Good [Go74] and Bicknell and Hoggatt [BiHo76] have shown that $\sum \frac{1}{F_{2^n}}$ is irrational - in fact,\[\sum \frac{1}{F_{2^n}}=\frac{7-\sqrt{5}}{2}.\]Badea [Ba87] proved that $\sum \frac{1}{F_{2^n+1}}$ is irrational. The sum $\sum \frac{1}{F_n}$ itself was proved to be irrational by André-Jeannin [An89] . The main problem has been proved for $c\geq 2$ by Badea [Ba93] . It remains open for $1<c<2$.
